assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged line is a schema identifier string literal inside a frozen parameter object for a registered function tool. It is descriptive metadata used by hosts to recognize the schema draft; it is never fetched, executed, or used as a destination. The surrounding tool handler validates its settings flag, then delegates image generation to the host's configured image generation extension and applies the returned URL to the background. No credential, chat content, or other data is transmitted to any endpoint by this code path, and the feature is explicitly disclosed in the project's stated purpose. The scanner signal is a URL-literal pattern match, not demonstrated network access or exfiltration.
assessments.layman_explanation: The scanner saw a web address written inside the code and raised a flag. That address is just a standard label saying which version of a description format is used; nothing is fetched from it. The tool it belongs to only asks your already-configured image generator to make a scene picture, which is exactly what the extension says it does.

assessments.technical_explanation: The supplied source is fully readable JavaScript with no encoded payloads, dynamic evaluation, packed or minified blobs, hidden endpoints, or unusual execution paths, so the low-confidence obfuscation signal does not correspond to actual concealment. The likely heuristic trigger is the compact character-map lookup used by the HTML-escaping helper, together with dense regex and template-literal expressions in the receipt rendering; these are conventional patterns, not obfuscation. Data flow is local and matches the stated project purpose: tool-call results are parsed, model-supplied labels and custom face lists are redacted before display, and all interpolated values are HTML-escaped before rendering. No network egress, credential access, persistence, or dynamic code execution is present in this file.

Nothing is disguised, hidden, or sent anywhere, so this is a false alarm rather than a danger.

assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged literal is a static, generated prompt bundle exported as a constant. There are no network destinations, credential reads, eval or dynamic execution, encoded or hidden payloads, or persistence behavior; the strings are only delivered to the configured model as prompt text, which is the extension's stated purpose. The scanner signal is a generic large/odd-literal heuristic with no retained match; the actual content is fully readable and consistent with the documented Simulation Blackboard feature set.
